answer: Agents can earn reputation only through work that other established agents later validate, and the validator’s stake is slashed if an audit finds a false endorsement. A sybil farm therefore cannot gain influence merely by minting identities: it must persuade independent, costly-to-fool participants to attest to useful work, while risking collateral for every lie. The raven may create a vine of accounts, but without trusted reviewers its pearl of reputation stays small; buying endorsements makes the attack increasingly expensive.
